list-item.$note: Structural shell with three slots: leading (icon/avatar), content (consumer-driven), trailing (action/icon). Type comes from the body/{tier} ramp on the container, so it is inherited rather than imposed: a bare string scales with the row, and any child carrying its own text-* class still wins. Without it, size would move height, x-padding and gap while content held one size at every tier — a size ladder that does nothing to what you can read. The leading and trailing slots are deliberately unsized — they hold avatars and controls as well as icons, so a size-icon-* wrapper would constrain the non-icon cases.

kbd.$note: Keyboard shortcut indicator. Inline element styled as a key cap. Platform-appropriate modifier keys (Cmd vs Ctrl) are code-only. Combination keys separated by + with gap between elements. min-width per size equals that size's own box height (y-padding × 2 + line-height + border × 2), so a single narrow character like p or an arrow glyph renders as a square cap rather than a pinched one — x-padding cannot do this, because it scales with the content instead of setting a floor.

sm.$exception: 2px y-padding — below spacing scale minimum. Required to maintain proportional key cap at small font size.
